_comment: Verified against a real running OpenClaw 2026.7.1-2 instance (openclaw config get), not just docs. Don't hand-edit API keys into this file — use openclaw models auth login --provider <id> or openclaw configure so credentials go through OpenClaw's own secret handling, not a checked-in file.

tools._comment: The 'messaging' profile only allowlists core built-in tool ids (see OpenClaw's tool-catalog.js: messaging.allow = coreToolIds + 'bundle-mcp') — it does NOT automatically include plugin-provided tools. Without alsoAllow below, every fieldops-tools call is invisible to the model at the actual agent-turn/tool-resolution step, even though the plugin itself loads fine and shows up in `openclaw plugins list`. This was silent for most of the build because it only surfaces once a real model call succeeds (auth failures short-circuit before tool selection) — first caught 2026-08-12 once a real DeepSeek key was added and a digest cron job replied with real content but couldn't call any tools.

media._comment: Turns on inbound voice-note transcription -- OpenClaw downloads the audio, transcribes it, and replaces the message body with the transcript before the reply pipeline runs (see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). Neither DeepSeek nor Anthropic/Claude (the two funded providers) can transcribe audio, hence OpenAI here specifically -- it's also the next fallback slot in agents.list[].model.fallbacks below, so this key does double duty. No API key in this file -- run `openclaw models auth login --provider openai` to add one.

image._comment: Turns on inbound photo classification -- fieldops-media still auto-files every photo instantly as type='photo' (unchanged, zero added latency), but with this on, the agent turn also sees a text description of the image and can call classify_document to upgrade the type to receipt/permit/contract/insurance_cert/disposal_ticket when it's clearly one of those. OpenAI pinned explicitly, same reasoning as audio above -- auto-detect would likely prefer Anthropic (ahead of OpenAI in bundled provider priority).
image.prompt: Describe this image. If it looks like a receipt or invoice, note any visible vendor name and total amount. If it's construction/landscaping equipment, note its condition. If it's a permit, contract, insurance card, or disposal ticket, say so plainly.

list.name: fieldops
list._comment: Model config is per-agent, not global — this is what keeps the personal 'main' agent's model settings untouched. `openclaw models set/fallbacks` don't support --agent; this has to be set via openclaw config patch against agents.list, as done here.
list._bootstrapComment: AGENTS.md outgrew OpenClaw's default 20000-char per-file bootstrap cap (it's ~29000 chars as of this increment, confirmed truncated in a live run's diagnostics) — raised per-agent here rather than globally, so 'main' keeps the default. bootstrapTotalMaxChars raised too since all 6 bootstrap files combined (~34000 chars) already exceed the default 60000 total once headroom for further AGENTS.md growth is counted.

plugins._comment: fieldops-tools loads from the repo path directly (plugins.load.paths) rather than a global `openclaw plugins install`, so editing the repo and restarting the gateway is enough — no reinstall step. Installing it a second time via `openclaw plugins install` creates a duplicate-id conflict (harmless-looking warning, but broke cron/isolated-session tool resolution in practice) — don't do both. fieldops-media, deepseek, and moonshot are separate ClawHub packages installed via `openclaw plugins install clawhub:@openclaw/<name>` / `openclaw plugins install ./plugins/fieldops-media`, tracked here for documentation only — this file doesn't reinstall them.

whatsapp._comment_groupPolicy: Group support (a shared dispatch group instead of/alongside 1:1 DMs) is real but not turned on yet -- see below for the config it needs once a real group exists. Leave 'disabled' until then.
whatsapp._comment_group_rollout: Once a WhatsApp group is created and the paired number is added to it: (1) set groupPolicy to 'allowlist', (2) groupAllowFrom needs every crew member's phone number who should be able to trigger the agent in the group -- this list is separate from the crew_members table and does NOT stay in sync automatically; update both whenever crew changes. (3) groups needs the real group JID, which isn't known until OpenClaw has seen a message from it -- send one test message first, then check gateway logs (--verbose) for 'from: <groupJid>'. requireMention: true is the recommended starting point (the agent only acts when pinged, rather than replying to every message in a work group) -- this can be flipped live later with '/activation always' sent as a plain message in the group by an allowlisted sender, no redeploy needed. See agent-workspace/AGENTS.md's 'Resolving who's messaging you' and 'confirm before you execute' sections for the per-sender safety rules a group requires that a 1:1 DM doesn't.
